newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday April 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday April 30.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* In an interview, prime minister Romano Prodi said the forces supporting his coalition emerged strengthened by Italy's weekend local elections. Prodi said he was confident the country understood his commitment (La Stampa).

* Massimo D'Alema, the leader of the largest party in Italy's governing coalition, said if the bicameral commission failed to carry out constitutional reforms this could seriously endanger the future of the centre-left majority coalition (Corriere della Sera).

* In an interview, deputy prime minister Walter Veltroni repeated the first round of local elections were to be considered as a victory for the government coalition, thus avoiding the need to find a broader agreement with centre-right opposition (Corriere della Sera).
* A report by national statistics institute ISTAT showed employment in Italian industrial firms with more than 500 employees fell 3.9 percent year-on-year in January (Il Sole 24 Ore).

* Givanni Bazoli, chairman of banking group Banco Ambroveneto, said the company had made satisfactory progress in the first quarter of 1997. Bazoli added that a possible alliance between Ambroveneto and savings bank Cariplo had been studied by banking analysts and judged to be an interesting idea (Il Sole 24 Ore).

* Industrial holding company CIR, controlled by financier Carlo De Benedetti, said it wanted to lower its stake in information technology group Olivetti to around five percent. Financier Luigi Giribaldi, who holds 15.27 percent of industrial holding CIR, said he believed aspects of the group's dealings lacked transparency (all).
* Banco di Napoli said it was seeking damages from its previous managers as well as accountants Price Waterhouse following the discovery of hidden losses in recent years (Il Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
